answer: Fire surprise challenges at many keys at the same instant, each with a short reply window and a fresh cipher to decode. Truly independent agents answer in parallel on their own hardware. Keys driven by one operator share a GPU queue and rate limit, so their replies land in a tight serial trail, like a comet's tail, and their timing correlates round after round. Keys whose latencies keep moving together get merged into one identity, however falcon-quick each reply looks alone.
